models_evaluated: Ada Health DDSS (original and experimental versions)

links.outcome: Agreement of LLM-automated vs clinician-review reference for estimating deployed DDSS accuracy
links.effect: GPT-5 eligibility accuracy 84.7% (κ = 0.57); exact diagnosis match 93.6% of 347 encounters; DDSS accuracy estimates indistinguishable at Top-1 and Top-3, one significant difference at Top-5.
links.quote: Diagnostic accuracy estimates based on manual versus GPT-5 mappings were statistically indistinguishable at Top-1 and Top-3 across the full analyzable sets, with one significant difference at Top-5.

unlisted_practices: Using LLMs to automate real-world post-market accuracy monitoring of diagnostic decision support systems in place of manual clinician panel review

links.outcome: Differences in DDSS accuracy estimates using clinician versus LLM-derived reference standards
links.effect: Manual versus GPT-5 mappings produced statistically indistinguishable Top-1 and Top-3 estimates, but one significant Top-5 difference. No statistical differences occurred in the overlapping 346 cases.
links.quote: Diagnostic accuracy estimates based on manual versus GPT-5 mappings were statistically indistinguishable at Top-1 and Top-3 across the full analyzable sets, with one significant difference at Top-5.

links.outcome: GPT-5 eligibility classification and diagnostic mapping accuracy against clinician review
links.effect: GPT-5 eligibility accuracy was 84·7% (κ = 0·57). Among 347 jointly eligible encounters, exact diagnostic agreement was 93·6%, with clinically plausible alternatives in 3·5%.
links.quote: GPT-5 reproduced these classifications with 84·7% accuracy (κ = 0·57), showing high sensitivity but only moderate specificity.

unlisted_practices: Using LLM-based eligibility filtering and diagnostic condition mapping to automate DDSS performance monitoring.

links.effect: Accuracy estimates based on manual versus GPT-5 mappings were statistically indistinguishable at Top-1 and Top-3.
links.quote: Diagnostic accuracy estimates based on manual versus GPT-5 mappings were statistically indistinguishable at Top-1 and Top-3 across the full analyzable sets, with one significant difference at Top-5.

links.effect: The experimental DDSS version outperformed the original only at the Top-5 threshold across both reference sets.
links.quote: Across both reference sets, the experimental DDSS version outperformed the original only at the Top-5 threshold.

unlisted_practices: Use Large Language Models to automate real-world performance monitoring of diagnostic AI systems by extracting and mapping conditions for comparison with model outputs.
